content:
The image is a brightfield microscopy shot at 20 µm scale showing fungal conidia with the following key features:

- **Multi-septate** (7-10 transverse septa visible), elongated/obclavate conidia
- A distinct **narrow beak-like apical cell** at one end tapering from a wider body
- **Light olive-tan to brown** coloration
- Multiple spores visible (one large central one, partial views at corners showing more rounded, multi-celled morphology)
- Spores forming in what appears to be a cluster/chain arrangement

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- The spore morphology is unambiguously *Alternaria*-type: obclavate, septate, beaked conidia
- Among the 19 classes, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** is the only one with explicit microscopic spore description: "light olive brown to dark brown, hand grenade-shaped with a shorter beaked apical cell on the terminal end" — the beak and olive-brown coloration match directly
- Early_Blight is also Alternaria (A. solani), but its class description only covers field symptoms (concentric rings, lesion color), not microscopy — this image appears to be a pathogen microscopy slide
- No other class (Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Septoria, etc.) produces this type of large, beaked, multi-septate conidium

The corner spores showing a more rounded, blocky multi-celled shape align with the "hand grenade-shaped" description. The central spore shows the characteristic beak. This is consistent with *Alternaria* conidia from stem canker infections.
